Definition: to enclose; hence (in a friendly sense) to crown, (in a hostile one) to besiege; also to wait (as restraining oneself)
BiblicalUsage: To enclose is to crown and surround, and strong bulls of Bashan compassed the sufferer round, and the psalmist asks to be brought out of prison, and Habakkuk says the wicked compass about the righteous so that wrong judgment goes forth, and Elihu says God has yet to speak on His behalf. The word holds the surrounding enemy and the surrounding God together: one encloses to crush, the other encloses to keep.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the bulls of Bashan are real, because the righteous are still compassed about by the wicked. I hold that the same word says God compasses His people too, and the enclosure of His presence is the safer one.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
